one_liner: AMZN +15.32% on 2.2x volume after AWS grew 36.7% (fastest in 18 quarters) and $496B backlog confirmed the $220B capex is demand-driven — RSI 71.6 and Wyckoff buying climax flag signal near-term digestion likely.

price_action.intraday_story: Gapped up from ~$235 prior close to $265 open, pushed to $273.23 intraday high then consolidated to close at $271.58. The 2.5% intraday range from high to close suggests some profit-taking into the gap, which is normal for a 15%+ earnings gap. The Wyckoff system flagged this as a 'buying climax' — high volume, strong close near the high. While bullish in isolation, buying climaxes often precede a short pause or pullback to absorb supply before the next leg.

news_catalyst.headline: Amazon Q2 2026: AWS grew 36.7% YoY (fastest in 18 quarters); $220B capex guided; $496B revenue backlog
news_catalyst.summary: CEO Andy Jassy delivered the key insight investors needed: Amazon's negative free cash flow is intentional and backed by $496B in contracted customer commitments — the capex is demand-driven, not speculative. AWS at $169B annualized run rate and both the AI and chips businesses crossing $25B annual run rates validated the AI infrastructure thesis. The Anthropic investment gain of $53.4B inflated reported EPS to $5.75 vs $1.82 consensus — operational earnings are much more modest. The market rewarded the contrast with Meta: Amazon has backlog, Meta does not. Stock up 15.32% on the day.

technical.summary:
RSI at 71.56 is technically overbought — the first time it's entered overbought territory in over a month. MACD histogram at +0.85 just turned decisively positive, confirming the momentum shift. However, the combination of overbought RSI and a Wyckoff buying climax flag is a signal to wait rather than chase.

The gap from ~$235 to $265 creates a gap fill zone that will likely act as support on any pullback. The ideal accumulate entry would be a volume dry-up pullback to the $255-262 zone over the next 5-10 sessions, where the gap low and prior resistance (now support) converge.

Analyst consensus target of $313 implies 15% additional upside even from today's elevated price, supporting the longer-term bull case while the technical picture argues for patience near-term.

wyckoff_narrative:
The buying climax event flagged today is consistent with Phase B of a new Accumulation structure, or alternatively the beginning of a Distribution Phase if the stock cannot hold above the gap. In the context of a 15% single-day move on fundamental catalysts, the Wyckoff buying climax is less a distribution warning and more a signal that supply is momentarily overwhelming demand at this price level.

For the accumulation thesis to remain intact, AMZN needs to see a subsequent Test of the buying climax level — ideally a 2-5 session pullback on declining volume that holds above the $255-262 gap fill zone. If instead volume remains elevated and price struggles to hold $265, watch for a potential UTAD setup.

valuation.summary: DCF is not meaningful for AMZN currently — the company is deliberately negative free cash flow ($111.63B TTM negative FCF) while investing in $220B of AI infrastructure. Preferred metric is price/operating cash flow: at 18x vs 5-year median of 20.75x, AMZN still trades below historical fair value on operating cash flow basis even after the 15% pop. Analyst target of $313 implies 15% further upside.

key_strengths: Operating margin hit all-time high of 12% this quarter
AWS at $169B annualized run rate, growing 36.7%
key_concerns: TTM free cash flow deeply negative (-$111.63B)
Raised $82B in debt over past year
Reported EPS of $5.75 massively overstated by $53.4B Anthropic gain
fundamentals.summary: Grade B reflects solid but not exceptional scoring — the negative FCF and elevated leverage weigh on the balance sheet pillar despite excellent operational performance. AWS reacceleration and all-time high margins are the fundamental highlights. The B grade does not capture the full operational strength.

risks: RSI 71.6 overbought — likely to pause or pull back before next leg
Gap fill to $262 is plausible and would be healthy; deeper fill to $245 would be concerning
Anthropic investment gains distort reported earnings — real operational EPS much lower
